newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian MTBE- Rangebound amid steady gasoline market.
newsitem.headline: Asian MTBE- Rangebound amid steady gasoline market.

text.p: Asian MTBE prices were rangebound amid steady gasoline prices as the market slowly returned to trade after the Lunar New Year holidays, traders said on Wednesday.
"Because gasoline is quite stable, MTBE is not softening," said one trader. "A push on gasoline is needed for MTBE to go beyond this range."
Traders assessed Singapore MTBE cost-and-freight (c-and-f) prices in a wide range of $280-$290 per tonne and free-on-board prices between $270-$275.
But trade was thin as the market took its time to warm up after the holiday.
"It is really, really quiet and demand is flat," said a producer.

With Taiwan only due to announce its April import tender next week, demand was limited mainly to a tender from Thai refiner Bangchak Petroleum Plc for 1,500 tonnes for delivery in March which closed February 17 and due to be awarded Thursday, traders said. They said the refiner was only considering offers below $280 c-and-f.

Another Thai refiner emerged early this week, but with a very prompt 1,000-tonne requirement which it bought from a Mideast supplier at $295 per tonne on a coast-and-freight (c-and-f) basis to Thailand.

In Singapore, only a U.S. major was reported to have bought a parcel at $280 per tonne c-and-f for delivery end March, while a Finnish producer sold a fob Singapore parcel was at $272-273 for March 1-15 lifting, heard heading to Indonesia.
Some blending demand was expected from Taiwan's reformate import tender for second-half March delivery which closed Tuesday.
Awards are expected on Thursday, but sources anticipated purchases of more than one cargo of the reformate with the 2.0-percent MTBE requirement at below $28.00 per barrel c-and-f Taiwan.
Taiwan made a disappointing purchase of only one cargo for the first half March arrival at $27.60 per barrel after receiving record high offers.
